title: Capt. Billy Bush and the Bush Settlement
summary: Capt. William "Billy" Bush organized the Bush Settlement on Lower Howard's Creek in Clark County, where Baptist families settled from 1784 around Providence Church.
bodyMarkdown:
Capt. [William "Billy" Bush](/people/#william-bush) organized the [Bush Settlement](https://explorekyhistory.ky.gov/items/show/824) on Lower Howard's Creek in what became Clark County. He located the land for himself and others. Beginning January 7, 1783, he piloted and marked the lines while [Daniel Boone](/people/#daniel-boone), acting only as a deputy surveyor, ran the first eleven surveys for him, totaling 6,147 acres.

Baptist families from Virginia and North Carolina began settling there in November 1784. Providence Church on Lower Howard's Creek became the center of the community.

Bush had come west with Boone's party in 1775, but his lasting mark is this Clark County settlement and its church.

## Kentucky today

The Lower Howard's Creek Nature and Heritage Preserve protects part of the creek valley. The [Col. John Holder](/stories/col-john-holder-at-lower-howards-creek/) story covers the station and mills at the creek's mouth. Much of the surrounding land is private; ask before you cross it.
